title: A recording shows in history the moment you stop it
goal: User 2026-09-28: 'When I record video, now there seems to be a delay before it shows in history as if we're processing it more. I do not want processing to interfere with the speed of the experience.' Something now runs between stopping a recording and its history entry appearing. Measure before changing anything: time from Stop to the file closed, to the history tile, and list every piece of work that runs in that gap (thumbnail, frame reads, waveform, captions/transcription, loudness, metadata, a re-encode) and whether the tile waits on it.
acceptance: Reproduced first: record 5 s and 60 s clips with system audio and mic; log timestamps for Stop, file finalised, history tile shown, thumbnail shown; compare with the commit from before the delay (git bisect if needed) and name the commit that introduced it
The history tile appears within 300 ms of the file being finalised, with a placeholder thumbnail if its real one is not ready
Nothing optional runs before the tile appears: waveforms, thumbnails, frame reads and any analysis run afterwards at background priority and never block the history, the editor opening, or playback
No transcription runs unless the person asks for captions (see the on-demand captions task)
A drill or test measures Stop-to-tile and fails above 300 ms; a perf note in the commit
